name: Autosomal Recessive Distal Renal Tubular Acidosis without Deafness
aliases: Distal Renal Tubular Acidosis Type 1 without Sensorineural Deafness

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Distal Renal Tubular Acidosis

criteria.description: Presence of hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis with normal anion gap
Inability to acidify urine to pH <5.5 despite systemic acidemia
No clinical or audiometric evidence of sensorineural deafness
Presence of hypokalemia or hypokalemic metabolic alkalosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis with normal anion gap, inability to acidify urine (pH >5.5), and absence of sensorineural deafness
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm mutations in ATP6V1B1 or ATP6V0A4 genes without associated deafness

searchTerms: acid-base imbalance with normal anion gap

pathognomonic.symptomName: Inability to acidify urine (urine pH >5.5 despite systemic acidemia)
searchTerms: urine stays less acidic despite blood acidosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Growth retardation due to chronic acidosis
searchTerms: poor growth from chronic acid buildup
growth delay due to long-term acidosis
growth failure related to acid-base imbalance

common.symptomName: Muscle weakness secondary to electrolyte imbalance
searchTerms: weak muscles due to mineral imbalance

occasional.symptomName: Mild hyperparathyroidism secondary to chronic acidosis
searchTerms: mild overactive parathyroid due to acidosis

rare.symptomName: Cardiac arrhythmias due to severe hypokalemia
searchTerms: heart rhythm problems due to hypokalemia
excessive urination due to kidney issue

laboratory: Hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis with normal anion gap
Elevated urine pH (>5.5) despite systemic acidemia
Elevated serum alkaline phosphatase in cases with bone involvement
imaging: Skeletal X-rays showing rickets or osteomalacia
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in ATP6V1B1 or ATP6V0A4 genes without associated deafness
other: Audiometric testing confirming absence of sensorineural deafness

distinguishingFeatures: Mutations in ATP6V1B1 gene commonly associated

redFlags: Severe hypokalemia causing muscle paralysis or cardiac arrhythmias
Failure to thrive or severe growth retardation in infancy
Progressive nephrocalcinosis leading to chronic kidney disease
references: Batlle DC, et al. Distal renal tubular acidosis. Kidney Int. 2012;81(6):589-597.
Orphanet: Autosomal recessive distal renal tubular acidosis without deafness - ORPHA:93609
Karet FE, et al. Mutations in the gene encoding B1 subunit of H+-ATPase cause renal tubular acidosis with sensorineural deafness. Nat Genet. 1999;21(1):84-90.
